ev.q: Reporting to NATRS decreased during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
The number of specimens with HAdV typing results reported varied annually during 2017–2019
six HAdV types accounted for 88.3% of all reported data
Annual reporting to NATRS increased from 389 specimens in 2017 to 562 in 2019.
17.0% of specimens were identified as outbreak-related
Among 1,451 typed specimens reported during 2017–2019, a total of 267 (18.4%) were outbreak-related.
The National Adenovirus Type Reporting System (NATRS) is a passive, laboratory-based surveillance system
Reporting to NATRS has declined since the COVID-19 pandemic
